label: Khawagi G157: Six-month carbamazepine level in the published indicator
title: Six-month carbamazepine level in the published indicator
statement: Mood stabilisers | Carbamazepine | Carbamazepine level | - | Every 6 months | [50]

plain_summary: The published indicator looks for a carbamazepine level every six months. Its use as a routine check in Australia needs clinical review. Convention proposed by Elicit, not yet ruled by the founder: Carbamazepine supplied ≥6 months with no level result in the previous 6 months.

needs_facts.meets: The latest dated carbamazepine concentration is older than 6 calendar months at the latest qualifying supply.

rule_for_models: At the latest supply of carbamazepine, assess only if dated supplies and directions support at least 6 months of ongoing treatment with the qualifying medicine and the record covers the interval. If the latest carbamazepine concentration is older than 6 calendar months, cite that line and supplies establishing duration as a possible monitoring gap, or cite those supplies and name the missing carbamazepine concentration if it is absent throughout. A dated carbamazepine concentration on or within the previous 6 calendar months gives no finding regardless of its value.
cannot_be_seen: Outside monitoring and supplies may be missing. A gap in this record cannot establish that care was missed. The indication for a drug level and the individual monitoring plan may be unknown.
ask_the_gp: Could you review whether a carbamazepine level is clinically indicated and whether one is already available?
